warning: Synthetic identifiers. Offline contract vectors only. Not a live job, deployment record, authorization receipt or qualified evidence. This route was proven against the real in-memory and AWS broker handlers with injected fake dependencies. No AWS deployment is claimed.

hashDefinition.serialization: JSON.stringify of {conversationId, prompt} plus {candidate} only when the request carries one, in that key order, unsorted, after schema parsing normalizes field order.
hashDefinition.note: requestId is the idempotency key, not part of the payload hash. Two different payloads under one requestId must conflict.

route.ownerIdentity: taken from the authenticated token, never from the request

404.meaning: no index entry for this owner, workspace and request; also returned for an unknown or non-owned workspace and for revoked project membership
404.caution: This does NOT prove the original submission never reached a worker. It must never trigger an automatic re-submission.

409.meaning: acceptance only: the requestId was reused with different content

503.meaning: the request index is dangling or corrupt, or storage failed; state is unknown
503.caution: Never reported as 404 and never carries the underlying message or a stored row.

vectors.name: task-without-candidate
vectors.description: Ungoverned task. Hash covers conversationId and prompt only.

vectors.name: task-with-candidate

vectors.name: task-with-candidate-non-ascii-prompt
vectors.description: Non-ASCII prompt. JSON.stringify emits these characters literally rather than as \u escapes; the hash is over that serialization encoded as UTF-8.

vectors.name: task-with-candidate-reordered-keys

vectors.name: task-with-candidate-changed-base-commit

request.prompt: Add All / Open / Done filtering. Preserve pagination and team isolation.
